paragraphs: Before they enter the forest, Narion shows the group some magic bracelets. “My fox will go ahead and check the path,” he says. “It can send us a message about what it sees. It only sends a message when there is danger. When the path is safe, it keeps looking and sends nothing.”

"Put on a bracelet to subscribe as an observer. Take it off to unsubscribe. Then you will get no more notifications. The fox will still do its job, and everyone who still wears a bracelet will still get the discovery."

Narion and Dre’Kaar put on their bracelets. Soon, the fox sees danger and sends both of them the same message. Narion plans a safer path. Dre’Kaar gets ready to protect the group. Each person chooses what to do. Later, Narion takes off his bracelet. The next time the fox sees danger, only Dre’Kaar gets its message.
imageAlt: The fox scouting with Narion in the forest
caption: One Subject publishes to many Observers
task: Build a class diagram. Let the fox act as a Subject that notifies each Observer through the Observer interface. The fox does not need to know their concrete classes.
concept: Subject keeps a list of observers and publishes notifications through notify(). The Observer interface defines update(); each concrete observer implements it and decides what to do with the discovery.
